name: Habakkuk
bio: Habakkuk the prophet complained to the LORD about the violence and injustice he saw going unpunished in Judah, asking how long he must cry out before God acted. The LORD answered that he was already raising up the Chaldeans (Babylonians) as an instrument of judgment — a response that troubled Habakkuk further, since this oppressive nation seemed even more wicked than those it would punish. Habakkuk then took his stand as a watchman to await the LORD's reply, and received the famous answer that "the righteous shall live by his faith," along with a series of woes pronounced against the proud and violent oppressor. The book closes with a psalm in which Habakkuk, despite dreading the coming devastation, declares he will rejoice in the LORD and trust him as his strength even if everything else fails (Habakkuk 1:1-3:19).
